title: Broken Climate Pledges and Europe’s Heat Wave

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，展示着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是...

sentences.en: A historic heatwave is crippling Europe just as two of the world's largest contributors to global warming are abandoning key commitments to limit emissions.
sentences.zh: 一场历史性的热浪正在席卷欧洲，而与此同时，全球两个最大的温室气体排放国却正在放弃限制排放的关键承诺。

sentences.en: My colleague, Samini Sengupta, on why the era of global cooperation on climate is starting to unravel.
sentences.zh: 我的同事萨米尼·森古普塔将为您解析，为何全球气候合作的时代正开始瓦解。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 今天是周二，

sentences.en: July 19th.
Samini,
sentences.zh: 萨米尼，

sentences.en: we wanted to talk to you because you're the international climate correspondent at The Times and it very much feels like we're experiencing a moment here that needs to be explained in terms of both climate policy and climate conditions on the ground.
sentences.zh: 我们想和你聊聊，因为你是《时报》的国际气候记者，现在的情况感觉就像我们正经历一个关键时刻，需要从气候政策和实地气候状况两个层面来加以解释。

sentences.en: So just to start, can you describe exactly what is happening right now in Europe?
sentences.zh: 那么，首先你能描述一下欧洲现在到底发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, people in Europe and the United Kingdom are living in the climate future now.
sentences.zh: 是的，欧洲和英国的人民现在正生活在气候的未来之中。

sentences.en: London is set to be one of, if not the hottest spot on the planet today.
sentences.zh: 伦敦今天注定会成为地球上最热的地方之一，如果不是最热的话。

sentences.en: Temperatures were forecast to hit 104 Fahrenheit for the first time.
sentences.zh: 据预测，气温将首次达到104华氏度（约40摄氏度）。

sentences.en: That's not just above normal.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是高于正常水平。

sentences.en: That is 30 degrees above normal.
sentences.zh: 这是比正常水平高出了30度。

sentences.en: Extremely hot.
sentences.zh: 极其炎热。

sentences.en: Unbearably hot, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，热得让人难以忍受。

sentences.en: So parts of England are hitting nearly 100 degrees Fahrenheit or peaking over 37 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰部分地区的气温正接近100华氏度，或者说超过了37摄氏度。

sentences.en: That's not normal.
sentences.zh: 这不正常。

sentences.en: But it is, you know, normal now.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，现在这成了常态。

sentences.en: Most homes are not built for this kind of heat anywhere in Europe.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲，大多数房屋都不是为这种高温而建造的。

sentences.en: In fact, most homes don't even have air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数家庭甚至连空调都没有。

sentences.en: Either do most schools.
sentences.zh: 大多数学校也是如此。

sentences.en: Some have canceled classes.
sentences.zh: 有些学校已经停课了。

sentences.en: It's way too hot to go outside.
sentences.zh: 外面实在太热了，没法出门。

sentences.en: Even if you go in the shade, it will still be too hot.
sentences.zh: 即使你躲在阴凉处，依然会觉得太热。

sentences.en: I was in London a couple of weeks ago and I walked across this bridge called the Hammersmith Bridge,
sentences.zh: 几周前我在伦敦，走过一座叫哈默史密斯桥的桥，

sentences.en: which is only open to pedestrians and cyclists right now because it's an old bridge in need of repair.
sentences.zh: 它现在只对行人和骑行者开放，因为这是一座需要维修的老桥。

sentences.en: And today I learned that the bridge was being wrapped in foil.
sentences.zh: 今天我得知，这座桥正在被锡箔纸包裹起来。

sentences.en: Where chains on all four corners of the structure have been wrapped in what essentially looks like tin foil you'd find in the kitchen at home.
sentences.zh: 桥梁结构四个角上的链条被包裹在看起来就像家里厨房用的锡箔纸里，

sentences.en: To prevent the structure from cracking in this heat.
sentences.zh: 以防止结构在这种高温下开裂。

sentences.en: One small airport in London, a runway closed for a couple of hours today because the runway was literally melting and apparently a small section of it lifted.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的一家小型机场，今天有一条跑道关闭了几个小时，因为跑道真的在融化，显然有一小部分路面翘了起来。

sentences.en: It's just very, very hot, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这真的非常、非常热，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's hard to get through everywhere, you know, in the tube.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在地铁里到处都很难受。

sentences.en: It's just absolutely sweltering everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都闷热得要命。

sentences.en: The railway lines have slowed down.
sentences.zh: 铁路运输已经减速了。

sentences.en: One of them is going to close tomorrow because in extreme heat, some of the tracks start to buckle.
sentences.zh: 其中一条线路明天就要关闭，因为在极端高温下，一些铁轨开始弯曲变形。

sentences.en: The way I look at it is people pay good money to go abroad to get this sort of weather.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，人们花大钱出国就是为了享受这种天气。

sentences.en: We get two days of it over here and the whole country comes to a standstill.
sentences.zh: 而我们这里只经历了短短两天，整个国家就陷入了瘫痪。

sentences.en: What does that say about us as a nation?
sentences.zh: 这说明了我们作为一个国家是什么样的情况？

sentences.en: This is not just in England, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不仅仅是在英格兰。

sentences.en: In France, several parts of France have hit record temperatures.
sentences.zh: 在法国，多个地区的气温都创下了历史新高。

sentences.en: This has affected some of the nuclear plants in France, where France gets a lot of its electricity from.
sentences.zh: 这影响了法国的一些核电站，而法国的大部分电力都来自这些核电站。

sentences.en: In Spain, one of the newspaper headlines that I saw a couple of days ago said that Spain was experiencing an avalanche of uncontrollable wildfires.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙，几天前我看到的一条新闻标题说，西班牙正经历一场无法控制的野火雪崩。

sentences.en: This, of course, exacerbated by the heat.
sentences.zh: 当然，这被高温加剧了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, from everything you're saying and from everything I have been reading,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从你所说的一切以及我所读到的一切来看，

sentences.en: it feels like not an exaggeration to say that many places in Europe right now are basically withering and melting.
sentences.zh: 说欧洲许多地方现在基本上正在枯萎和融化，这并不夸张。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is all supersized by climate change.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切都被气候变化放大了。

sentences.en: We will see much more of this every summer.
sentences.zh: 我们每年夏天都会看到更多这样的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And all of this is occurring at a moment when two of the most important players in climate policy and two of the biggest polluting forces in the world are taking pretty big steps away from the commitments that they have made to tackle warming temperatures.
sentences.zh: 而这一切发生之时，全球气候政策中最重要的两个参与者，也是世界上两个最大的污染源，正在大幅背离他们为应对气温升高所做出的承诺。

sentences.en: And that would be the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那就是美国，

sentences.en: and Europe itself.
sentences.zh: 以及欧洲本身。

sentences.en: And I want to begin with Europe, because Europe, as you have told us, Amini, has been seen as the great hope for climate activists and researchers.
sentences.zh: 我想先从欧洲谈起，因为正如你告诉我们的，萨米尼，欧洲一直被气候活动家和研究人员视为巨大的希望所在。

sentences.en: The reason why Europe is so important is that it contains some of the biggest industrialized countries on Earth.
sentences.zh: 欧洲之所以如此重要，是因为它拥有地球上一些最大的工业化国家。

sentences.en: And then if you add the United Kingdom to that, you know, you're talking about some of history's biggest emitters.
sentences.zh: 如果你再加上英国，你谈论的可是历史上最大的几个排放国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Europe, as well as the U.K., had set out some really ambitious climate plans.
sentences.zh: 而且欧洲以及英国，确实制定了一些非常雄心勃勃的气候计划。

sentences.en: So the European Union has enshrined in law a promise to cut its greenhouse gas emissions by more than half by 2030.
sentences.zh: 欧盟已将到2030年将温室气体排放量减半以上的承诺写入法律。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Very similar law in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 英国也有非常类似的法律。

sentences.en: So really ambitious, short-term climate plans.
sentences.zh: 所以这些短期气候计划确实非常雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And these commitments were really celebrated for their boldness when they were made.
sentences.zh: 这些承诺在做出时，确实因其大胆而受到赞誉。

sentences.en: But then, of course, came the war in Ukraine, which upended the entire global energy supply and threatened almost every economy in Europe.
sentences.zh: 但随后，乌克兰战争爆发了，它颠覆了整个全球能源供应，并威胁到欧洲几乎每一个经济体。

sentences.en: The Russian invasion of Ukraine has absolutely challenged Europe's climate plans.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵绝对挑战了欧洲的气候计划。

sentences.en: Europe is in a very tricky position because it gets a lot of its energy from Russia.
sentences.zh: 欧洲处于一个非常棘手的境地，因为它的大部分能源来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Specifically, gas.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是天然气。

sentences.en: The Russian invasion of Ukraine squeezed the energy supply in Europe, and it really accelerated a debate over which way Europe will go.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵挤压了欧洲的能源供应，并真正加速了一场关于欧洲未来走向的辩论。

sentences.en: Will it kind of double down on the development of its renewable energy sources so they are no longer as dependent on the gas from Russia?
sentences.zh: 它是会加倍投入可再生能源的开发，从而不再那么依赖俄罗斯的天然气吗？

sentences.en: Or will they accelerate efforts to get gas from anywhere other than Russia?
sentences.zh: 还是会加速从俄罗斯以外的任何地方获取天然气的努力？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's the debate that Europeans are having right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是欧洲人现在正在进行的辩论。

sentences.en: And they made a decision a couple of weeks ago that seems to put their thumb on the get gas from anywhere other than Russia button.
sentences.zh: 几周前他们做出了一个决定，似乎让他们倾向于选择“从俄罗斯以外的任何地方获取天然气”这一选项。

sentences.en: Explain that decision.
sentences.zh: 解释一下那个决定。

sentences.en: So two weeks ago, the European Parliament voted to classify gas as a, quote-unquote, green fuel.
sentences.zh: 两周前，欧洲议会投票决定将天然气归类为“所谓的”绿色燃料。

sentences.en: Gas is actually a fossil fuel.
sentences.zh: 天然气实际上是一种化石燃料。

sentences.en: It's not green.
sentences.zh: 它并不绿色。

sentences.en: Its principal component is methane, which is a gas that warms up the Earth's atmosphere really, really quickly.
sentences.zh: 它的主要成分是甲烷，这是一种能非常、非常迅速地使地球大气变暖的气体。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So why would the EU reclassify a not-green energy source as green?
sentences.zh: 那么欧盟为什么要将一种非绿色能源重新归类为绿色能源呢？

sentences.en: What was the argument for doing that?
sentences.zh: 这样做的理由是什么？

sentences.en: Aha.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: Well, it basically greenlights a bunch of new gas projects and makes them eligible for cheap loans and, in some cases, public subsidies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它基本上为一系列新的天然气项目开了绿灯，并使它们有资格获得低息贷款，在某些情况下还能获得公共补贴。

sentences.en: So in reality, this means more new gas projects, and it means that Europe will prolong its reliance on gas.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这意味着更多新的天然气项目，也意味着欧洲将延长对天然气的依赖。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so what's the practical impact of that going to be when we think about the climate goals that you reminded us of earlier for Europe?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们想到你之前提醒我们的欧洲气候目标时，这在实践中会产生什么影响？

sentences.en: The implication of this vote is pretty big because, on the one hand, it allows more gas projects to be built, not just for, like, the next two, three years,
sentences.zh: 这次投票的影响非常大，因为一方面，它允许建造更多的天然气项目，不仅仅是未来两三年，

sentences.en: but potentially for the next 20, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 而是可能长达未来20到30年。

sentences.en: But it also sends a signal to other countries that one of the, you know, these rich industrialized nations are willing to prolong their reliance on fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 但它也向其他国家发出了一个信号，即这些富裕的工业化国家之一，愿意延长对化石燃料的依赖。

sentences.en: So it's much harder than for European countries to say to emerging economies, oh, you know, don't burn your coal or don't develop your oil fields because it's bad for the climate.
sentences.zh: 因此，欧洲国家就很难再对新兴经济体说，哦，你知道，不要燃烧煤炭，或者不要开发油田，因为这对气候不利。

sentences.en: Right, because we, too, are embracing fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为我们自己也在拥抱化石燃料。

sentences.en: We, who are responsible for most of the emissions already in the atmosphere,
sentences.zh: 我们这些已经对大气中大部分排放负责的国家，

sentences.en: whose impacts you are seeing right now in the form of extreme weather that we've just been talking about.
sentences.zh: 其后果你现在正以我们刚才谈到的极端天气的形式看到。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's turn now to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在让我们转向美国。

sentences.en: We have talked, Simini, about the Supreme Court ruling that represented a major setback to the Biden administration's attempts to cut U.S.
sentences.zh: 萨米尼，我们已经在节目中谈到了最高法院的裁决，这对拜登政府削减美国排放的努力构成了重大挫折。

sentences.en: emissions on the show.
sentences.zh: 那项裁决基本上削弱了环保署（EPA）乃至行政部门开展这项工作的权力。

sentences.en: That decision basically gutted the powers of the EPA and thus the executive branch to do that work.
sentences.zh: 就在几天前，总统的气候计划感觉真的被乔·曼钦参议员正式且不可逆转地扼杀了。

sentences.en: And then just a few days ago, it really felt like the president's climate plan was officially and kind of irreversibly killed off by Senator Joe Manchin.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 记住，拜登总统上任时，宣布了一项相当雄心勃勃的气候议程。

sentences.en: Remember, when President Biden took office, he announced a pretty ambitious climate agenda.
sentences.zh: 但上周四晚些时候，西弗吉尼亚州的参议员乔·曼钦表示，他不会支持那项已经大幅缩水的气候立法。

sentences.en: But late last Thursday, Senator Joe Manchin of West Virginia said he wouldn't support what had become a vastly whittled down piece of climate legislation.
sentences.zh: 他的民主党同僚与他进行了长达18个月的谈判，试图通过一项气候法案。

sentences.en: His fellow Democrats were negotiating with him for the better part of 18 months to get a climate law passed.
sentences.zh: 最终，他说他不会支持。

sentences.en: In the end, he said he wouldn't go for it.
sentences.zh: 这确实打击了在美国通过气候立法的任何希望，

sentences.en: And this really was a blow to any hopes of getting climate legislation passed in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 以至于拜登总统出来承认，在气候问题上采取立法行动已不可能。

sentences.en: so much so that President Biden came out and acknowledged that legislative action on climate wasn't possible.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以，一位承诺将美国重新置于全球减排努力中心的美国总统，现在不得不说，抱歉，伙计们，游戏结束了。

sentences.en: So an American president who has pledged to put the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: back at the center of global efforts to reduce global warming is now having to say, sorry, folks, game over.
sentences.zh: 记住，他上任总统后做的第一件事就是重新加入《巴黎协定》，当时有很多关于“美国回来了”的讨论。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 最近的这次挫折确实让“美国回来了”这种言论成了一个笑话。

sentences.en: And remember, one of the first things he did when he took office as president is he rejoined the Paris Agreement, and there was lots of talk about America is back.
sentences.zh: 为了把这一切放在一个视角下看，当我们思考气候变化这个更大的问题，以及我们每个人脑海中都有的那个数字时，美国乃至欧洲在几乎同时倒退，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: This latest setback really makes a mockery of that America is back rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 1.5摄氏度，我们希望在未来几年将气温升幅限制在这个数字内？

sentences.en: And just to put this all into perspective, what will it mean for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: and, to a degree, Europe to backpedal as they have almost simultaneously when we think about the larger question of climate change and this number we all have in our head,
sentences.zh: 所以记住，当我们结束格拉斯哥国际气候谈判时，你听到世界各国领导人说，是的，

sentences.en: 1.5 degrees Celsius, that we want to limit temperature rise to in the coming years?
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是到本世纪末，将全球气温升幅控制在比工业化时代初期高出1.5摄氏度以内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的北极星，1.5摄氏度。

sentences.en: So remember, when we came out of the international climate talks in Glasgow, you heard world leaders saying, yes,
sentences.zh: 你从美国听到了这一点。

sentences.en: our goal is to keep global temperatures from rising past 1.5 degrees Celsius by the end of this century as compared to the beginning of the Industrial Age.
sentences.zh: 你从欧洲领导人那里也听到了这一点。

sentences.en: That was their North Star, 1.5 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 我们现在的气温已经升高了1.1摄氏度。

sentences.en: You heard this from the United States.
sentences.zh: 我说的是今天全球平均气温与工业化时代初期相比。

sentences.en: You heard this from European leaders.
sentences.zh: 所以，美国未能通过气候立法，欧洲说，是的，我们要让化石燃料在能源结构中再保留一段时间，所有这些都使得将升温控制在1.5摄氏度以内变得非常、非常困难，甚至是不可能的。

sentences.en: We are already 1.1 degree Celsius hotter.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm talking about global average temperature today compared to the beginning of the Industrial Age.
sentences.zh: 所以这个十年，本应是应对气候变化的十年，你谈到过这一点，我们的同事科拉尔·达文波特也谈到过，

sentences.en: So the failure of the United States to pass climate legislation, Europe saying, yeah, we're going to have fossil fuels in the mix for a while longer, all of this is making it very,
sentences.zh: 2020年代本应是世界采取行动的时期。

sentences.en: very difficult, if not impossible, to keep 1.5 degrees within reach.
sentences.zh: 仅仅过了两年半，这个十年看起来就已经非常像是一场失败了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时形成了一些共识，即世界需要非常迅速地减少对化石燃料的依赖，比如在这个十年内完成。

sentences.en: And so this decade, which was supposed to be the decade of combating climate change, you've talked about this, our colleague Coral Davenport has talked about this,
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: the 2020s were going to be the period where the world got its act together.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么变化的话，那就是世界似乎正在加深对化石燃料的依赖。

sentences.en: This decade is already starting to very much look like a failure just two and a half years in.
sentences.zh: 这使得减缓气候变化变得非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: You know, there was some consensus developing that the world needed to very swiftly reduce its reliance on fossil fuels, like do it in this decade.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: That isn't happening.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: If anything, the world seems to be deepening its reliance on fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: That makes slowing down climate change really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的《交易手册》峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话实况。

sentences.en: I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么随着美国

sentences.en: federal government walking away from climate policy and Europe backsliding on it, what will be the biggest sources of action in the coming years?
sentences.zh: 联邦政府背离气候政策，而欧洲也在这一问题上出现倒退，未来几年最大的行动源头会是什么？

sentences.en: Who will take up this mantle?
sentences.zh: 谁将接过这面大旗？

sentences.en: Will it be local government in places like the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 会是像美国这样的地方政府吗？

sentences.en: Will it be global corporations?
sentences.zh: 会是全球性大公司吗？

sentences.en: Will it be smaller countries?
sentences.zh: 会是较小的国家吗？

sentences.en: What does your reporting tell us?
sentences.zh: 你的报道告诉了我们什么？

sentences.en: So first off, I think it's important to acknowledge that in public opinion, poll after poll, a majority of Americans say the government should do more on climate.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为很重要的一点是，在公众舆论中，民调一次又一次地显示，大多数美国人认为政府应该在气候问题上采取更多行动。

sentences.en: So can the White House do more?
sentences.zh: 那么白宫能做得更多吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes, there are things it can do with executive action without legislative approval.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，有些事情它可以通过行政手段在无需立法批准的情况下完成。

sentences.en: So the White House can regulate tailpipe pollution in cars and trucks, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，白宫可以监管汽车和卡车的尾气污染。

sentences.en: It can set pollution regulations from power plants.
sentences.zh: 它可以制定发电厂的污染法规。

sentences.en: It can focus on methane regulations.
sentences.zh: 它可以专注于甲烷法规。

sentences.en: Many of these things are likely to be challenged in court.
sentences.zh: 其中许多举措很可能会在法庭上受到挑战。

sentences.en: And so that is likely to slow down those kinds of regulations.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能会减缓这些法规的实施速度。

sentences.en: So who's left?
sentences.zh: 那么还剩下谁呢？

sentences.en: Well, there's state action.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有各州的行动。

sentences.en: There are big states like California that have set pretty ambitious state-level laws.
sentences.zh: 像加利福尼亚州这样的大州已经制定了相当雄心勃勃的州级法律。

sentences.en: So, for example, in California, by 2035, all new car sales must be electric.
sentences.zh: 例如，在加利福尼亚州，到2035年，所有新车销售必须是电动汽车。

sentences.en: By 2045, all of California's electricity must come from zero emissions sources like solar and wind.
sentences.zh: 到2045年，加州所有的电力必须来自太阳能和风能等零排放能源。

sentences.en: And in the state of New Mexico, for example, which has a lot of coal, the governor has set aside some money for local communities to be helped as coal plants are being retired.
sentences.zh: 以新墨西哥州为例，该州拥有大量煤炭，州长已经拨出了一些资金，用于在煤电厂退役时帮助当地社区。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's a scattershot approach, if you will, little things that might add up to something.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一种零散的方法，如果可以这么说的话，一些小事加起来可能会有所作为。

sentences.en: But all of these local and state actions really cannot replace national climate legislation, which seems impossible at the moment.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些地方和州的行动确实无法取代国家层面的气候立法，而这在目前看来是不可能的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, beyond the U.S., are there places where you foresee impactful actions in the coming years?
sentences.zh: 那么，在美国之外，你预见未来几年哪些地方会有影响力的行动？

sentences.en: And let's turn to Europe, for example, which we talked about a bunch in the first half of this episode.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向欧洲，我们在本集前半部分讨论了很多关于欧洲的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know that we talked about this green designation for a gas project, which is, you know, infuriating to climate advocates.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道我们讨论过这个天然气项目的绿色标签，这让气候倡导者感到愤怒。

sentences.en: But look, Europe still has a law on its books to reduce emissions by more than half by 2030.
sentences.zh: 但你看，欧洲仍然有法律规定到2030年将排放量减少一半以上。

sentences.en: So, Europe is continuing to do quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，欧洲仍在做相当多的工作。

sentences.en: For example, it has a law that says no new internal combustion engine cars to be sold by 2035.
sentences.zh: 例如，它有一项法律规定，到2035年不得销售新的内燃机汽车。

sentences.en: It is pressing all commercial buildings to put solar panels on their roofs.
sentences.zh: 它正在推动所有商业建筑在屋顶安装太阳能电池板。

sentences.en: It is rolling out a lot of wind.
sentences.zh: 它正在大力推广风能。

sentences.en: In some countries, like Denmark, two-thirds of its electricity comes from wind energy.
sentences.zh: 在丹麦等一些国家，三分之二的电力来自风能。

sentences.en: And then in European cities, you're also seeing quite a bit of action.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲城市，你也能看到相当多的行动。

sentences.en: So, in London, for example, it is super expensive to bring an old polluting car into the city center.
sentences.zh: 例如在伦敦，驾驶老旧污染严重的汽车进入市中心费用极高。

sentences.en: And you're seeing that in many other European cities, these congestion taxes, restrictions on internal combustion engine cars coming into the city,
sentences.zh: 你在许多其他欧洲城市也能看到这种情况，这些拥堵税、对进入市区的内燃机汽车的限制，

sentences.en: really reducing a big source of emissions, which is from transportation.
sentences.zh: 确实减少了一个主要的排放源，即交通运输。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, whereas the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，与美国相比，

sentences.en: approach will be local and it will be scattershot, Europe's will be more transnational, more integrated, and seemingly more impactful.
sentences.zh: 美国的方法将是地方性的、零散的，而欧洲的方法将更具跨国性、更整合，看起来也更有影响力。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Europe does still have something of a plan, but that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，欧洲确实还有某种计划，但这还不够。

sentences.en: You need to have all of the big emitters, including the U.S., rapidly reducing greenhouse gas emissions in order to avert climate catastrophes like the ones we're seeing now.
sentences.zh: 你需要所有排放大国，包括美国，迅速减少温室气体排放，以避免我们现在看到的那些气候灾难。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about that, the idea of climate catastrophes in the wake of everything you have just explained.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我们谈谈这个，在你刚才解释了一切之后，关于气候灾难的想法。

sentences.en: Because the worst impacts of climate inaction are probably never going to be felt by places like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为气候不作为带来的最坏影响，可能永远不会被像美国这样的地方感受到，

sentences.en: and the countries of Europe, places that you have described as the global North Simini.
sentences.zh: 以及你所描述的全球北方国家，Simini。

sentences.en: And when we use that phrase, what we really mean is, you know, mostly wealthy countries that can afford to adapt to climate change.
sentences.zh: 当我们使用这个短语时，我们真正指的是，你知道，主要是那些有能力适应气候变化的富裕国家。

sentences.en: The heat wave in Europe, yes, it's very bad, but as you just said, the U.K.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的热浪，是的，非常严重，但正如你刚才所说，英国

sentences.en: is wrapping its bridges in foil.
sentences.zh: 正在用箔纸包裹桥梁。

sentences.en: It can afford to do that.
sentences.zh: 它负担得起这样做。

sentences.en: It can afford air conditioning if people want it.
sentences.zh: 如果人们需要，它负担得起空调。

sentences.en: But in the global South, which is traditionally countries without those resources, the ability to adapt is nowhere near as great.
sentences.zh: 但在全球南方，传统上是那些缺乏这些资源的国家，适应能力远没有那么强。

sentences.en: So what will be the impact of the decisions that are now being made in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，现在在美国做出的决定，

sentences.en: and in Europe on those countries in the global South?
sentences.zh: 以及在欧洲做出的决定，对全球南方的那些国家会有什么影响？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So by global North, we mean the rich industrialized countries that are responsible for most of the historic emissions.
sentences.zh: 所以，全球北方指的是那些对大部分历史排放负责的富裕工业化国家。

sentences.en: Countries in the global South aren't responsible for most of those emissions, but their people, particularly their poorest people,
sentences.zh: 全球南方的国家并不对大部分排放负责，但他们的人民，特别是最贫困的人民，

sentences.en: are the ones that are feeling the impact most seriously, most acutely.
sentences.zh: 是感受影响最严重、最剧烈的人。

sentences.en: So in India and Pakistan, for example, you had these off-the-charts prolonged heat waves.
sentences.zh: 例如在印度和巴基斯坦，你们经历了这些破纪录的长期热浪。

sentences.en: In low-lying island nations, in the Pacific, in South Asia, in the Caribbean, you have countries that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 在太平洋、南亚、加勒比地区的低洼岛国，你们有这样的国家，你知道，

sentences.en: losing farmland every time there's a storm surge because global sea levels are rising.
sentences.zh: 因为全球海平面上升，每次风暴潮都会失去农田。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what really matters when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，当美国

sentences.en: can't get climate legislation passed is that millions of vulnerable people suffer.
sentences.zh: 无法通过气候立法时，真正重要的是数百万脆弱的人民正在受苦。

sentences.en: And so that's why in the next few months,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在接下来的几个月里，

sentences.en: you're likely to hear louder calls from people in the global South who say they need to get paid for the repeated losses and damages that they're seeing in their countries because of inaction by these rich industrialized countries.
sentences.zh: 你可能会听到来自全球南方的人们发出更响亮的呼声，他们说由于这些富裕工业化国家的不作为，他们需要为在自己国家看到的反复损失和损害获得赔偿。

sentences.en: And when they say get paid, they essentially mean reparations, payments from wealthy countries who inflicted the climate damage that is now occurring in the global South.
sentences.zh: 当他们说获得赔偿时，他们本质上指的是赔款，即从造成现在发生在全球南方的气候损害的富裕国家那里获得支付。

sentences.en: In polite diplomatic language, Michael, they don't call it reparations.
sentences.zh: Michael，在礼貌的外交语言中，他们不称之为赔款。

sentences.en: They call it losses and damages, loss and damage.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为损失和损害，损失与损害。

sentences.en: And you're going to just hear increasing calls for loss and damage funding.
sentences.zh: 你只会听到越来越多关于损失和损害资金的呼声。

sentences.en: We've also seen a resistance to that sort of separate pot of money from countries in the global North, including in Europe and the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们也看到全球北方国家，包括欧洲和美国，对那种单独的资金池存在抵触情绪。

sentences.en: So it's been a can kick down the road for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 所以这多年来一直是一个被踢皮球的问题。

sentences.en: But I suspect that in the climate talks coming up in Egypt, you're going to hear a lot more about this.
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑在即将于埃及举行的气候谈判中，你会听到更多关于这个问题的讨论。

sentences.en: But to me, won't that end up in many ways pitting country against country, region against region,
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这难道不会在许多方面导致国家对国家、地区对地区的对立吗？

sentences.en: the North against the South in a way that very much seems at odds with the spirit of global cooperation that has really been essential to the idea of getting climate change contained?
sentences.zh: 北方对南方，这似乎与全球合作的精神非常不符，而这种精神对于遏制气候变化的想法至关重要？

sentences.en: I mean, what you're describing is a scene in which increasingly the global South looks at the inaction of the global North and says, we're furious with you, pay up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你所描述的是一个场景，全球南方越来越多地看着全球北方的不作为，并说，我们对你们很愤怒，付钱吧。

sentences.en: That does not seem like a recipe for everyone holding hands and saying, we're going to limit our fossil fuels and our carbon output.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不像是一个让大家携手合作，说我们要限制化石燃料和碳排放的配方。

sentences.en: Look, there was a brief moment of international cooperation in 2015 when all of the nations of the world came together and agreed to the Paris Climate Accord.
sentences.zh: 看，2015年曾有过短暂的国际合作时刻，当时世界各国齐聚一堂，同意了《巴黎气候协定》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was predicated on some really crucial things.
sentences.zh: 那是基于一些非常关键的事情。

sentences.en: One was that rich industrialized countries would quickly reduce their own emissions.
sentences.zh: 一是富裕的工业化国家将迅速减少自身的排放。

sentences.en: They would set their targets and they would do it.
sentences.zh: 他们会设定目标并付诸实施。

sentences.en: That hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 这并没有发生。

sentences.en: That would give money to poor countries to shift away from, you know, polluting fuels and to adapt to the impacts of climate change.
sentences.zh: 二是他们会给贫穷国家钱，让他们从污染燃料转向其他能源，并适应气候变化的影响。

sentences.en: That money hasn't come forward.
sentences.zh: 那笔钱并没有到位。

sentences.en: So there is a serious lack of credibility.
sentences.zh: 所以存在严重的信誉缺失。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Precisely at this moment when we are seeing accelerating climate impacts.
sentences.zh: 恰恰在我们看到气候影响加速的这一刻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this whole system is built on credibility.
sentences.zh: 而整个系统是建立在信誉之上的。

sentences.en: So what happens when that credibility starts to go away?
sentences.zh: 那么当这种信誉开始消失时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Where does it leave this global project, this existential project of trying to contain rising temperatures?
sentences.zh: 这让这个全球项目，这个试图遏制气温上升的生存项目处于什么境地？

sentences.en: It leaves that project in tatters.
sentences.zh: 它让这个项目支离破碎。

sentences.en: Well, Simini, appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，Simini，感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Michael。

sentences.en: On Monday afternoon, the Secretary General of the United Nations delivered a dire warning to world leaders about rising temperatures,
sentences.zh: 周一下午，联合国秘书长向世界各国领导人发出了关于气温上升的严厉警告，

sentences.en: calling it a, quote, climate emergency.
sentences.zh: 称之为“气候紧急状态”。

sentences.en: We have a choice, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们面临一个选择。

sentences.en: Collective action or collective suicide.
sentences.zh: 集体行动，还是集体自杀。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the heat wave in Europe is expected to continue today,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，欧洲的热浪预计今天将持续，

sentences.en: with temperatures in London forecast to reach 102 degrees Fahrenheit and temperatures in Paris forecast to reach 106.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的气温预计将达到102华氏度，巴黎的气温预计将达到106华氏度。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 一个月的时间，让你越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能得到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to another day.
sentences.zh: 以下是你还需要知道的另一件事。

sentences.en: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 早上好，女士们，先生们。

sentences.en: I'm going to speak to you about the unspeakable.
sentences.zh: 我将要对你们谈论一件难以启齿的事情。

sentences.en: About this defendant's goal-directed, planned, systematic murder, mass murder,
sentences.zh: 关于这个被告目标明确、有计划、系统性的谋杀，大规模谋杀，

sentences.en: of 14 children, an athletic director, a teacher, and a coach.
sentences.zh: 杀害了14名学生、一名体育主管、一名老师和一名教练。

sentences.en: On Monday, prosecutors in Florida delivered their opening statement in the sentencing trial of
sentences.zh: 周一，佛罗里达州的检察官在量刑审判中发表了开场陈述，

sentences.en: Nicholas Cruz, the gunman who killed 17 people at a high school in Parkland, Florida, four years ago.
sentences.zh: 被告是四年前在佛罗里达州帕克兰一所高中杀害17人的枪手尼古拉斯·克鲁兹（Nicholas Cruz）。

sentences.en: These brutal murders occurred at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, and it happened on February the 14th, 2018.
sentences.zh: 这些残忍的谋杀案发生在佛罗里达州帕克兰的玛乔丽·斯通曼·道格拉斯高中，发生于2018年2月14日。
zh_words: 玛乔丽·斯通曼·道格拉斯

sentences.en: Cruz, who has pleaded guilty to 17 murders and 17 attempted murders for those he injured, faces either the death penalty or life in prison without the possibility of parole.
sentences.zh: 克鲁兹对17项谋杀罪和17项谋杀未遂罪表示认罪，他面临死刑或终身监禁且不得假释的判决。

sentences.en: And police are crediting an armed bystander with ending a mass shooting at a mall in Greenwood, Indiana by killing the suspected gunman shortly after he opened fire.
sentences.zh: 警方称赞一名武装旁观者在印第安纳州格林伍德的一家购物中心结束了一场大规模枪击事件，他在枪手开火后不久将其击毙。

sentences.en: Many more people would have died last night if not for a responsible armed citizen that took action very quickly within the first two minutes of the shooting.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为一位负责任的武装公民在枪击发生后的最初两分钟内迅速采取行动，昨晚会有更多人死亡。

sentences.en: His actions were nothing short of heroic.
sentences.zh: 他的行为堪称英雄。

sentences.en: The suspect, who was armed with a rifle, a pistol, and 100 rounds of ammunition, killed three people before the bystander shot him to death.
sentences.zh: 这名嫌疑人携带了一支步枪、一把手枪和100发弹药，在被旁观者击毙前杀害了三人。

sentences.en: He engaged the gunman from quite a distance with a handgun, was very proficient in that, very tactically sound.
sentences.zh: 他用手枪在相当远的距离与枪手交火，表现得非常熟练，战术非常稳健。

sentences.en: And as he moved to close in on the suspect, he was also motioning for people to exit behind him.
sentences.zh: 当他移动以靠近嫌疑人时，他还示意人们在他身后撤离。

sentences.en: To our knowledge, he has no police training and no military background.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，他没有受过警察训练，也没有军事背景。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon Johnson,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Michael Simon Johnson制作，

sentences.en: Asta Chaturvedi, Diana Nguyen, and Will Reed.
sentences.zh: Asta Chaturvedi、Diana Nguyen和Will Reed参与制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Mark George, contains original music by Marian Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: Davis-Lynn和Mark George编辑，包含Marian Lozano的原创音乐，由Chris Wood进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Landsberg创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和Sarah Koenig将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
